title: 1. Article 1 – Name and Territory of India

blocks.content:
Article 1 states:
“India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States.”

IMPORTANT POINTS:
• India is called both **India** and **Bharat** in the Constitution.
• The word **Union** was chosen deliberately.

WHY ‘UNION’ AND NOT ‘FEDERATION’?
• Indian federation is NOT the result of an agreement among states.
• States cannot secede from the Union.
• The Union is indestructible, but states can be reorganized.

EXAM TRAP:
Q. India is described as what in Article 1?
✔ Union of States
India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States.

rows: Not the result of an agreement among states
Result of an agreement among states

items: Article 1 describes India as a 'Union of States', NOT a 'Federation of States'.
States in India do not have any right to secede from the Union.
The Union is indestructible, whereas the states are destructible/reorganizable.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Constitution recognizes both 'India' and 'Bharat' as official names.
India is specifically designated as a 'Union of States' rather than a federation.
The Indian federation is not the result of an agreement among independent states.
States do not have the right to secede from the Union.
The Union of India is indestructible, though internal state boundaries can be reorganized.
